sections.report:
Walk (working notes). The image is 1280×800, about one screen, so I worked from the whole image.

First read: the eye lands on "Tell us about your project", then moves to the white form card. It reads as the contact page of a small design studio, and it feels calm, plain and templated. The submit action at the bottom of the form ("Send message", ~541,526) has no button shape, so the eye finds no place to finish.

Job (assumed): a contact page where prospective clients send a project enquiry.

- One-sentence purpose: yes.
- Image and headline make one idea: yes (there is no main image, so the headline carries it alone).
- Every element does a job: yes (the card groups the form, and the header rule separates the nav).
- One mood and era: yes.
- Copy finished: yes.
- Each kind of element looks the same everywhere: yes (nav and footer links are both blue and underlined, and the three fields match).
- Mood fits the message: yes.
- Headings name their content: yes.

No line is `no` or `unsure`, so step 5 has no entries to open.

**Section.** The whole piece: applies.

**Findings**
None.

(For the director, outside this section: "Send message" at about (541,526) is plain body text with no fill, border or link styling, so it doesn't read as the submit control. The checklist says to file control defects under Interface, so I've left it there. It's the biggest problem on the page.)

**What's working.**
- **The intro copy makes a specific promise.** "We read every message and reply within two working days" gives a time frame people can hold the studio to. "Include a budget range and a rough timeline" tells them exactly what to write, so the empty Message box is less daunting.
- **The page holds together as one piece.** It uses one typeface family, one blue for all links, a grey page with a single white card, and three identically styled fields. Nothing looks borrowed from elsewhere.

**Checklist.** The whole piece: 8 lines, 8 yes, 0 no, 0 unsure

sections.report:
**Section.** What matters first: applies.

**Findings**
None.

**What's working.**
- The headline "Tell us about your project" (x≈56–368, y≈120–205) is the one dominant element. It is the largest type on the page, bold, near-black, and has open space around it. The eye starts there with no competition. The logo (bold, about 20 px) and the blue nav links (top right) are clearly a step down, so the header doesn't fight it.
- The few text levels are each easy to tell apart. The headline is large and bold. The intro paragraph (y≈224–292) is regular weight and a softer grey. The field labels ("Your name", "Email address", "Message") are small, bold and dark, and the footer links are small blue underlined text. Where sizes sit close together, as with the intro and the labels, weight and colour separate them, so no two levels look like a mistake. The headline is set apart from the body by weight and colour as well as size.

**Couldn't judge from a still.** The submit action, "Send message" (x≈541–653, y≈516–536), looks like plain body text with no button shape, fill or colour. It has less visual weight than any field label. This section doesn't cover controls, so I didn't file it here. It should go under Interface, and the director should weigh it there.

**Checklist.** What matters first: 3 lines, 3 yes, 0 no, 0 unsure

**Section.** Arrangement and space: applies.

**Findings**
1. **Do all blocks, pictures included, take their edges and the gaps between them from one grid, so column lines and gutters repeat down the page?** and **Do the main divisions of the frame follow one proportion, such as halves, thirds, or the golden section, rather than arbitrary splits?** One problem answers no to both lines. The header and footer set the page margins at x=56 and x=1224; the logo and footer links sit on 56, and the "Contact" nav link ends at 1224. The body follows the left margin only. The intro column runs from 56 to about 440. The form card runs from x≈509 to x≈1068, about 156 px short of the right margin, so its right edge lines up with nothing above or below it. The body also splits the 1168 px content width into about 385 / 69 / 559 px, which is not halves, thirds or any other clear ratio.

   What the viewer sees: the header spans the full width, but the content stops early. A strip about 212 px wide sits empty at the right (x 1068–1280), under the nav. The page looks unfinished, as if a third column failed to load or the card was sized by eye. Nothing there stops anyone from using the form, but it makes a design studio's own page look less crafted, and a studio's page is itself a sample of its work.

   Why: Müller-Brockmann, *Grid Systems in Graphic Design*, says every block takes its edges from one grid, and a block whose edges match no other was placed by eye. The proportion point is my taste: no approved source makes it a rule.

   Fix: put the body on the same columns as the header. Either run the card's right edge to x=1224, or build the content on a 12-column grid across 56–1224 so the intro and the card get a clear split (for example 5 + 7 columns, or 4 + 8). If the form is meant to stay narrow for shorter fields, narrow the whole content area and the header with it, so all three share one right edge.

   Mark: convention (grid), taste (proportion). Weight: minor.

**What's working.**
- Spacing inside the form groups its parts. Each label sits about 8 px above its own field, and about 31 px separates one field from the next label. The pairs read without effort and no label is ambiguous.
- One left edge carries the page. The logo, headline, body copy and footer links all start at x=56, and inside the card the labels, fields and "Send message" all start at x=541. The two left lines are exact, with no near-misses, which keeps the page calm.

**Checklist.** Arrangement and space: 13 lines, 11 yes, 2 no (one grid governs the page; main divisions follow one proportion), 0 unsure

I checked the one borderline line against its reference entry. Here is the report.

**Section.** Text: applies.

**Findings**
1. **Do headings and captions break at phrase boundaries, never between a number and its unit or inside a name?** No. The headline at about x 56–368, y 122–205 breaks as "Tell us about your / project". That separates "your" from the noun it belongs to and leaves "project" alone on the second line. The reader takes in "Tell us about your…" as an unfinished phrase, then has to pick up the key word by itself on the next line. Visually the heading also becomes a long line over a stub, which makes the block lopsided above the three even intro lines. The rule is Bringhurst, *The Elements of Typographic Style*, §2.4, but the entry marks the heading part as unconfirmed, so treat this as common sense. To fix it, break at the phrase boundary ("Tell us about / your project") or widen the heading's box so it sits on one line. Either way, check it at the other breakpoints. Taste. Weight: minor.

**What's working.** The intro paragraph (x 56–436, y 225–292) is set well. It is plain upright type at a comfortable size, in a dark grey that reads clearly on the light grey background. The space between lines is easy, and the lines run about 43–46 characters, which suits a three-line note. The copy is also specific: it promises a reply "within two working days" and tells the reader what to include (a budget range and a rough timeline). The type hierarchy is tight: one sans-serif family in roughly four sizes. Bold carries the field labels and the heading, and no sizes sit so close together that they collide.

**Checklist.** Text: 30 lines, 29 yes, 1 no (headings break at phrase boundaries)

I found one problem in the Color section. The page's only colour, a blue, goes on the nav and footer links and never on "Send message", so the main action has no colour to mark it.

**Section.** Color: applies.

**Findings**
1. **Is strong, saturated color kept to a small share of the area, with most of the area neutral or muted?** The blue is small in area, as it should be. But all of it goes on the four nav links (about x 943–1224, y 30) and the three footer links (x 56–246, y 762). It never reaches the one action the page exists for. "Send message" at about (541–653, 526) is plain near-black text: no fill, no border, no colour. A visitor who finishes the message has nothing to tell them where to click. Their eye is pulled to the blue nav and footer links instead, which lead away from the form. Apple HIG and Material Design 3 both say to save the accent for the main action and interactive states. Here the accent is on the links and missing from the action that matters most.
   - Fix: make "Send message" a solid button in the accent blue (or a darker shade of it), with white text. Keep the nav and footer links quieter so they don't compete with it.
   - Type: defect, because it slows and can lose the viewer at the moment of conversion. The button's missing shape and its target belong to the Interface section; this finding is only about the colour.
   - Weight: major.

**What's working.**
- **Restrained palette:** one cool neutral range (near-black text, pale gray page, white card and fields) and one blue. The page reads calm and orderly, and colour isn't wasted on decoration.
- **Light and dark structure:** near-black headings and labels against white fields and a pale ground give the page a clear structure that would survive in grayscale. The links are underlined as well as blue, so their meaning doesn't depend on colour alone.

**Checklist.** Color: 9 lines, 8 yes, 1 no (strong colour kept to a small share, here as an accent spent on links instead of the main action)

**Section.** Pictures: skipped. The page has no photos, illustrations or icons. The only thing that could count as a mark is "Fernwick Studio" at the top left (about x 56–213, y 20–44). It is plain bold text in the same typeface as the rest of the page, so it falls under the Text section, not this one. It has plenty of space around it and is a single dark colour, so nothing about it would be a Pictures finding anyway.

**Findings**
None.

**Checklist.** Pictures: skipped

sections.report:
I've finished the walk; writing up the report now.

**Section.** Interface: applies. The page has nav links, a three-field contact form, a submit action and footer links.

**Findings**
1. **Is exactly one button styled as the primary action, with every other action styled lower? / Does every control look like what it does, buttons pressable, fields typeable, and links marked by more than color?**
   - **Where:** "Send message" at about 541–653 × 516–536.
   - **What the viewer meets:** it is plain dark text in the body size, with no fill, border, underline or colour. It reads as a caption or leftover label, not the page's only action. Someone who has filled in three fields has to guess what to click. Next to the blue underlined nav and footer links, it is the least clickable-looking thing on the page.
   - **Why:** the page has no primary action at all (Material Design 3, Apple HIG, "Buttons"). Clickable text that looks like a label is a fault; this one is common sense, since the NN/g source does not state this rule outright. If it is really a button whose styles failed to load, that would explain it, but the still shows no sign of that.
   - **Fix:** give the main action the shape of a button, with a fill or a border, so it looks like something to click. Make it the one strongest-looking control in the card, with a hit area of at least 24 px tall (WCAG 2.5.8). As drawn, only the roughly 20 px text line shows as a target.
   - Defect. Weight: major.
2. **Does the screen show where the user is and what is happening?**
   - **Where:** the nav at the top right. "Contact" (1168–1224, y≈30) is drawn exactly like Work, Services and About.
   - **What the viewer meets:** nothing in the nav says this is the Contact page. Only the H1 does, and it doesn't use the word "contact".
   - **Why:** Nielsen heuristic 1, and Laubheimer, "Menu-Design Checklist" (NN/g), guideline 5: indicate the user's current location in the menu.
   - **Fix:** mark the current item with one clear cue, such as a bolder weight, a bar, or dropping the link styling.
   - Convention. Weight: minor.
3. **Are required or optional fields marked?**
   - **Where:** the labels "Your name", "Email address" and "Message" at x=541, y=163/254/345.
   - **What the viewer meets:** no asterisk or "optional" anywhere. The viewer can't tell whether, say, the name is needed. They probably assume all three are, which is likely true, so the cost is small here.
   - **Why:** Budiu, "Marking Required Fields in Forms" (NN/g).
   - **Fix:** asterisk each required label and explain it once at the top of the form, or put "(optional)" after any optional field.
   - Convention. Weight: minor.
4. **Do input borders, control edges, and meaningful icons reach 3:1 contrast against what is next to them?**
   - **Where:** the three field borders (541–1035, at y 180–224, 271–315 and 362–482).
   - **What the viewer meets:** the borders are a light blue-grey on white. They look to be around 2.5:1, just under the WCAG 1.4.11 minimum. The fields still read as fields at normal vision, but they may fade for low-vision users or on weak screens.
   - **Why:** WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11.
   - **Fix:** measure the border colour against white. If it is below 3:1, darken it one step.
   - Convention. Weight: minor.

**What's working.**
- Every field has its own short bold label directly above it, closer to its field than to the one before. That is the textbook layout, and none of them relies on a placeholder.
- The nav and footer links are blue and underlined, so they are marked by more than colour and are easy to tell apart from body text. That is also why the unstyled "Send message" stands out as wrong.

**Couldn't judge from a still.**
- Focus indicators on the fields, the submit control and the links. The field borders are light, so check that focus adds a clear 2 px, 3:1 ring.
- Whether "Send message" is a real `<button>` and how big its hit area is.
- Validation and error messages after submit, and the success state.

**Checklist.** Interface: 33 lines, 28 yes, 4 no (one primary action styled as primary; controls look like what they do; current location shown; required fields marked), 1 unsure (focus indicator 2 px at 3:1). The input-border line is also counted as no in the findings above. Final tally: 27 yes, 5 no (one primary action; controls look like what they do; input borders at 3:1; current location shown; required fields marked), 1 unsure (focus indicator).
